links.outcome: Data leakage from oversampling before train-test split in prior pipeline
links.effect: Prior work reported 96% accuracy with leakage; corrected pipeline with oversampling only on training data achieved 86.76% test accuracy and weighted F1 of 0.8684.
links.quote: Our prior work achieved 96% accuracy using a Random Forest Classifier on 19 features from the Kaggle PCOS dataset; however, that pipeline contained a data leakage issue RandomOverSampler was applied before the train-test split and relied on ultrasound-derived features unavailable outside a clinical setting.

unlisted_practices: Restricting model inputs to home-accessible features for consumer deployment
Stateless inference with no user data storage

links.effect: Prior Random Forest reported 96% accuracy, but RandomOverSampler was applied before the train-test split.

links.effect: Decision threshold tuning at 0.40 raises PCOS-positive recall to 0.89.
links.quote: Decision threshold tuning at 0.40 raises recall for the PCOS-positive class to 0.89, appropriate for a screening tool where false negatives carry greater clinical cost.

links.effect: Logistic Regression test accuracy was 86.76% and weighted F1-score 0.8684, but differences were within sampling variability.
links.quote: Evaluated on a 75/25 stratified split with 5-fold cross-validation, Logistic Regression achieves the highest test accuracy of 86.76% and weighted F1-score of 0.8684 achieves the highest test F1 among the five classifiers evaluated, though differences are within sampling variability at this test set size.
